title: Neurodiagnostic Technology
author: Dayone Koo
_comment: PROGRAM EVALUATION of a program NOT YET OFFERED: Foothill College x TOP 121200 (Electro-Neurodiagnostic Technology), a two-year A.S. in partnership with UCSF, first cohort expected fall 2027 (Mountain View Voice, September 2026). Foothill has no COCI award, no awards, no enrollment and no courses for it yet, so this def uses the program-not-yet-offered fields (planned_awards, wage_note, crosswalk_chain, extra_colleges + programs + supply_scope). Destination: crosswalk(121200) = {25-1071, 29-2099, 99-9999}; the derivation rule drops 29-2099 as ALL_OTHER, so the destination is AUTHORED with the CIP chain as justification — TOP 1212.00 -> CIP 51.0903 -> SOC 29-2099, whose detailed O*NET occupation 29-2099.01 Neurodiagnostic Technologists is what the program prepares for. The demand section carries the COE figure for the 29-2099 bucket (Bay: 510 openings/yr) with one sentence placing 29-2099.01 inside it. Comparators are the two California colleges with active awards under the TOP, Orange Coast (A.S. 08657, OC region) and San Diego Mesa (A.S. 38642 + CoA 38643, SD/I region), so the supply section is statewide and draws no regional openings rule. Their courses are read from their Course Outlines of Record (Coast CCD CourseLeaf catalog; SDCCD CurriQunet META All Fields report). live_postings from tools/jobs/scrape_jobs.cjs 29-2099.01 94022 50 (7 hits; the 3 neurodiagnostic-titled ones kept, 4 polysomnography titles set aside). competencies: O*NET 29-2099.01 description; K/S/A from occupations.competencies for 29-2099 (the .01 specialty's ratings). TOP PROVENANCE: no official record assigns Foothill's program a TOP code yet — COCI (export 2026-08-27) has no Foothill program under 121200 in any status and the college's page names only the degree. 1212.00 is INFERRED: it is the Taxonomy of Programs' code for the discipline and the code both existing programs (08657, 38642) are approved under. The lede and chain_note say 'would be classified'; confirm against Foothill's COCI submission when it appears. UCSF POSTINGS: UCSF (the program's partner) never appears in CareerOneStop for 29-2099.01 within 25 miles of 94143, nor under EEG/neurodiagnostic/neuromonitoring keywords; its careers portal (careers.ucsf.edu, one portal for UCSF Health and campus) lists two current roles — EEG Technologist, Night Shift (UCSF Health, Oakland, posted 2026-07-09, req 4982) and Sr. EEG Technologist (UCSF Health, San Francisco, posted 2026-08-10, req 7209) — found by searching the portal in a browser (its list API refuses plain requests). They carry source=careers.ucsf.edu and lead the table as the partner's. Two UCSF polysomnographic roles (April 2026) were set aside. DEMAND VINTAGE 2025–2030: demand figures re-read against the Centers of Excellence 2025–2030 release (2026-09-18 refresh).
chain_note: The Chancellor's Office classifies electro-neurodiagnostic technology as TOP 1212.00. Orange Coast and San Diego Mesa run California's two existing programs under that code, and Foothill's will carry it once approved. From there the state's crosswalk leads through CIP 51.0903 to SOC 29-2099, the residual category for health technologists and technicians not listed separately. Within it O*NET names the occupation this program prepares students for: 29-2099.01, Neurodiagnostic Technologists.

lede: This evaluation assembles labor-market supply and demand evidence for Foothill College's planned Neurodiagnostic Technology program, an associate degree that would be classified under TOP 121200: regional demand for the occupation it is designed for, the award and enrollment trends of the California colleges already offering the program, and how their courses align with the work of that occupation.
demand_note: Neurodiagnostic Technologists (O*NET 29-2099.01) are reported within SOC 29-2099, Health Technologists and Technicians, All Other. [According to the Centers of Excellence](https://datastudio.google.com/u/0/reporting/c01114ab-6bc3-4529-bace-e933fe293b86/page/1v72D), this classification has roughly 510 openings a year in the Bay Area.

curriculum_note: O*NET maintains a set of detailed work activities that identify the competencies central to each job. Foothill's courses are not yet written, so as a point of reference we map the two California programs that already exist: the associate degrees at Orange Coast and San Diego Mesa. Each course is read against the work activities of Neurodiagnostic Technologists as its Course Outline of Record (COR) describes it.
employer_note: UCSF Health is the program's founding partner. [According to UCSF](https://www.ucsf.edu/news/2026/07/432201/how-fill-shortage-specialists-als-epilepsy-and-stroke), it has committed $170,000 in start-up funding to the two-year associate degree, which begins in fall 2027 at Foothill's Sunnyvale center. UCSF Health and UCSF Benioff Children's Hospitals will serve as clinical training sites, alongside Stanford Hospital, Kaiser Permanente, Highland Hospital and UC Davis Medical Center. Three of those clinical partners post the roles listed above: Stanford Health Care, Kaiser Permanente and Alameda Health System, which runs Highland Hospital.
